subject.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold

question: Should `loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay: false` remain a narrow opt-out for only the Codex PreToolUse loop-detection subprocess, or is it now the supported opt-out for both PreToolUse and PostToolUse loop-detection relays?
rationale: This changes the meaning of an existing user configuration setting, and source-level correctness cannot establish the intended compatibility promise for installations that already use it.

options.title: Preserve the prior narrow switch contract
options.body: Keep PostToolUse outcome relay behavior independent of the existing PreToolUse-specific setting, or provide an explicitly named compatible alternative.

options.title: Adopt the broader relay opt-out
options.body: Accept that `false` disables both loop-detection relays, retain the updated docs, and record the setting's broadened semantics as an intentional compatibility change.

recommendation.title: Preserve the prior narrow switch contract
recommendation.body: Keep PostToolUse outcome relay behavior independent of the existing PreToolUse-specific setting, or provide an explicitly named compatible alternative.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is a public configuration-contract decision for the Codex harness.
